trial_title: SMART Watch Facilitated Early Discharge in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement
brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to observe conduction disturbance, daily activity level, heart rates, oxygen saturation in patients who underwent Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement (TAVR) and to evaluate the utility of the HUAWEI Watch (HUAWEI Technologies Co., Ltd., Shenzhen, China) for the potential early warning sign of changes in multiple biometric parameters including heart rate, rhythm, oxygen saturation, activity, and sleep in patients following TAVR. eligibility_table.clinical_question: Is the patient at least 18 years old?

eligibility_table.criterion: Be willing and able to provide informed consent to participate in the study;
eligibility_table.justification: The patient is capable of providing informed consent as there is no indication of cognitive impairment.

eligibility_table.criterion: Not share HUAWEI Watch, HUAWEI phone with anyone else;
eligibility_table.justification: There is no information provided about sharing devices, so it cannot be determined.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Has the patient shared their HUAWEI Watch or HUAWEI phone with anyone else at any time?

eligibility_table.criterion: Patient has severe aortic stenosis with echocardiographically derived criteria: mean gradient > 40mmHg or maximum velocity greater than 4.0 m/s or an initial aortic valve area of < 1.0 cm2;
eligibility_table.justification: The patient has severe aortic stenosis, likely meeting the echocardiographic criteria based on the provided conditions.

eligibility_table.criterion: Patient who undergoing elective transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement.
eligibility_table.justification: The patient is undergoing elective transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement as indicated by their severe aortic stenosis.

eligibility_table.criterion: Severe complications of TAVR, such as death, and conversion to SAVR;
eligibility_table.justification: There is no information on whether the patient has experienced severe complications from TAVR.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Did the patient experience any severe complications, such as death or conversion to surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR), within 30 days post-transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR)?

eligibility_table.criterion: Life expectancy is less than 12 months due to non-heart disease (such as cancer, chronic liver disease, chronic kidney disease, or chronic end-stage lung disease, etc.);
eligibility_table.justification: The patient's life expectancy due to heart disease is uncertain; other non-heart disease factors are not mentioned.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have a documented life expectancy of less than 12 months due to non-heart disease conditions?

eligibility_table.criterion: Severe dementia (cannot sign research informed consent, cannot take care of themselves or complete the study visit);
eligibility_table.justification: There is no information provided regarding the patient's cognitive status or ability to care for themselves.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have a documented diagnosis of severe dementia as defined by a score of ≤10 on the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE)?

eligibility_table.criterion: The investigator believes that the patient is not suitable to participate in the study or complete the follow-up prescribed by the protocol from other medical, social and psychological aspects;
eligibility_table.justification: The investigator's opinion on the patient's suitability is not provided.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Does the patient have a documented history of non-compliance with medical treatment or follow-up appointments in the past year?

eligibility_table.criterion: The patient is currently participating in another randomized study.
eligibility_table.justification: There is no information indicating the patient is currently participating in another randomized study.
eligibility_table.clinical_question: Is the patient currently enrolled in any other randomized clinical trial?
